title: Chicken noodle soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook gently for 8 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken stock, add the thyme and bring to a simmer. Lower in the whole chicken thighs, then wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, the thickest part reaches 74°C and the juices run clear.
Lift the chicken onto a board and shred it with two forks. Remove the thyme stalks from the pot.
Bring the soup back to the boil, add the noodles and cook for 3–4 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming hot. Serve scattered with parsley, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the noodles for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, reheat until piping hot and cook fresh noodles in it.

title: Minestrone
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, courgette and oregano and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cannellini beans and pasta and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender.
Add the kale or cabbage for the last 3 minutes until wilted. Season with the salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with basil, if using.

To batch cook, freeze the soup without the pasta for up to 3 months, then reheat until steaming hot and cook the pasta in it. Leftovers with pasta keep in the fridge for 2 days but the pasta will soften.

title: Tomato and basil soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8–10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, stock and sugar. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrot is completely tender.
Take off the heat, add most of the basil leaves and blend with a stick blender, or carefully in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Season with the salt and pepper and reheat until steaming. Serve topped with the remaining basil.
This soup freezes well: cool, then freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

title: Butternut squash soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the squash and stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the squash is very tender when pierced with a knife.
Blend with a stick blender, or carefully in batches in a blender, until velvety smooth. Add a splash of water if it's too thick.
Season with the salt and pepper, reheat until steaming and serve with a swirl of coconut milk, if using.
To batch cook, cool and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat from thawed until piping hot, stirring well.

title: Pea and mint soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add the potato and garlic, pour in the stock and bring to the boil. Simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the frozen peas and simmer for 3–4 minutes until just tender and still bright green.
Take off the heat, add the mint leaves and blend with a stick blender, or in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice, salt and pepper, and reheat gently if needed. Serve straight away to keep the colour fresh.
This soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Leek and potato soup
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the leeks and onion, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft but not browned.
Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then add the potatoes and stock.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, or leave some texture if you prefer.
Stir in the milk, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming without boiling. Serve scattered with chives, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the milk for up to 3 months. Potato soups can thicken on freezing, so thin with a little milk or water when reheating until piping hot.

title: French onion soup
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and stir to coat.

Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until starting to soften, then add the sugar, turn the heat to low and cook for 35–40 minutes more, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are soft, sticky and deep golden brown.
Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then sprinkle over the flour and stir for another minute.

Gradually pour in the stock, stirring and scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pot. Add the thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the herbs and season with the salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Grill the baguette slices on a baking tray for 1–2 minutes each side until crisp, then top with the Gruyère and grill until bubbling.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and float two cheesy baguette slices on top of each to serve.
To batch cook, freeze the soup without the bread and cheese for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot and make the cheesy topping fresh.

title: Creamy mushroom soup
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the mushrooms and thyme and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and are golden. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Scoop out a ladleful of mushrooms and set aside. Blend the rest with a stick blender until smooth, then return the reserved mushrooms for texture.
Stir in the double cream, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming without boiling. Serve scattered with parsley, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the cream for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot, then stir in the cream.

title: Carrot and coriander soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and ground coriander and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrots, potato and stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Add most of the fresh coriander and blend with a stick blender, or in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Season with the salt and pepper, reheat until steaming and serve topped with the remaining coriander.
This soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

title: Mexican black bean soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and red pepper and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the black beans, chopped tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Blend about half the soup with a stick blender, leaving plenty of whole beans for texture.
Stir in the lime juice and salt, then taste and adjust. Serve topped with coriander and avocado, if using.
To batch cook, cool and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.
